questions.question: How should CSV rows be parsed? The vendor files could have descriptions containing commas (e.g. "Coffee Shop, Inc.") which a naive comma-split would break on.

options.label: Hand-rolled parser (Recommended)
options.description: Write a small parser that handles quoted fields, matching the codebase's existing no-dependency, hand-rolled style (e.g. TransactionRepository's pipe-delimited parsing). No pom.xml change.

options.label: Add Apache Commons CSV
options.description: Add a well-tested third-party CSV library dependency to pom.xml. More robust against edge cases (embedded newlines, escaped quotes) but introduces the project's first non-JavaFX/JUnit dependency.

options.label: Backend only (Recommended)
options.description: A CSV importer class plus repository integration and unit tests, following this repo's test-first pattern. No UI changes.

options.label: Backend + UI
options.description: Also add a file-picker/import button to the existing JavaFX transaction view so a user can trigger the import from the app.

# CSV Transaction Import

## Context

The Personal Finance App currently only supports manual, one-row-at-a-time transaction entry (`TransactionEntryView`). Real-world usage means importing bank/vendor exports, and those exports aren't standardized — header names and column layouts vary (`Date` vs `Transaction Date`; a single signed `Amount` vs separate `Debit`/`Credit` columns; `Category` is often missing). The goal is to let a user pick a CSV file and import it into their transaction history, tolerating format variation and bad rows without crashing or losing the rows that *are* valid.

Two decisions were confirmed with the user up front:
- **Apache Commons CSV** (new dependency) instead of a hand-rolled parser, so quoted fields with embedded commas (e.g. `"Coffee Shop, Inc."`) parse correctly.
- **Backend + UI**: a real "Import CSV" button in the existing JavaFX transaction screen, not just a backend class.

The design follows conventions already established in this codebase: `Transaction`/`TransactionRepository`'s skip-and-continue error handling for malformed rows, the plain-POJO JavaFX view style with a single status `Label` for all feedback (no dialogs), and the existing use of Java records for small data carriers (`GoalContribution.java` already uses one, so introducing more records here is consistent, not novel).

## Approach

### 1. Dependency
Add Apache Commons CSV to `personal-finance-app/pom.xml`:
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
    <artifactId>commons-csv</artifactId>
    <version>1.11.0</version>
</dependency>
```

### 2. New small data types
- `TransactionDraft.java` (record): `(LocalDate date, TransactionType type, String categoryName, BigDecimal amount, String description)` — everything needed to create a `Transaction` except the `id`. This is the seam between the importer and the repository.
- `TransactionCsvImportException.java`: unchecked, for **whole-file** failures only (unreadable file, empty file, required columns entirely missing). Never used for a single bad row.

### 3. `TransactionCsvImporter.java` (new)
Public API:
```java
public final class TransactionCsvImporter {
    public record RowError(long rowNumber, String reason) {}
    public record ImportResult(List<TransactionDraft> rows, List<RowError> errors) {}
    public ImportResult importFile(Path csvFile) { ... } // throws TransactionCsvImportException for file-level problems
}
```
Takes only a `Path`, returns only data — no dependency on `TransactionRepository`/`DataPaths`, so it stays trivially unit-testable and keeps CSV concerns out of the repository.

**Header alias resolution**: read Commons CSV's detected header names, normalize (trim + lowercase), and match against alias lists:
| Canonical field | Aliases | Required? | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|
| date | `date`, `transaction date` | yes | file-level error |
| amount | `amount` | yes, unless debit/credit present | — |
| debit / credit | `debit`, `credit` | yes (both), unless amount present | — |
| description | `description` | no | `""` |
| category | `category` | no | `"Uncategorized"` |

If both `Amount` and `Debit`/`Credit` are present, prefer `Amount`. If neither Date nor an amount source resolves, throw `TransactionCsvImportException` before processing any rows.

**Date parsing**: try `yyyy-MM-dd` (ISO) then `M/d/yyyy`; row error if both fail.

**Amount/sign logic**:
- Signed `Amount`: negative → `EXPENSE` (abs value), positive → `INCOME`; zero is a row error (sign is ambiguous).
- `Debit`/`Credit`: exactly one of the two non-blank → `EXPENSE`/`INCOME` respectively; both blank or both filled → row error.
- Strip `$` and `,` before parsing numbers (handles `$1,234.56`).

**Per-row errors**: wrap each row's extraction in `try { ... } catch (RuntimeException e)` — same idiom as `TransactionRepository.load()` — collect a `RowError` and continue (plus keep a `System.err.println` for parity with existing logging). A file that becomes structurally corrupt mid-stream stops iteration and returns whatever parsed successfully, rather than propagating — the importer must never crash the app.

### 4. `TransactionRepository.java` — add bulk insert
`add()` persists (full file rewrite) on every call; importing N rows one-at-a-time would mean N rewrites. Add:
```java
public List<Transaction> addAll(List<TransactionDraft> drafts) {
    List<Transaction> added = new ArrayList<>();
    for (TransactionDraft draft : drafts) {
        added.add(new Transaction(nextId++, draft.date(), draft.type(), draft.categoryName(),
                draft.amount(), draft.description()));
    }
    transactions.addAll(added);
    persist();
    return added;
}
```

### 5. `TransactionEntryView.java` — Import CSV button
Add `Button importCsvButton` to the existing `FlowPane` in `buildTransactionManagement()`, placed after `deleteButton` and before the `status` label (status stays last, per existing convention). On click: open a `FileChooser` (extension filter `*.csv`), obtain the `Window` from the event source (`((Node) e.getSource()).getScene().getWindow()` — no constructor changes needed), call `new TransactionCsvImporter().importFile(...)`, then `transactionRepository.addAll(result.rows())`, then update `status` with a summary like `"Imported 18 of 20 rows. 2 skipped: Row 5: Unparseable date '13/40/2026'; ..."`. Catch `TransactionCsvImportException` around the whole thing and show `"Import failed: " + ex.getMessage()` in `status`. Reuse the existing status `Label` rather than adding new UI surface (no `Alert`/`TextArea` used anywhere else in the app). No changes needed to `MainApp.java`.

### 6. Tests
- `TransactionCsvImporterTest.java` (new, same `@TempDir` + `Files.writeString` convention as `TransactionRepositoryTest`): standard `Date/Amount` headers, `Transaction Date` alias, `Debit/Credit` columns, missing `Category` defaults to `Uncategorized`, mixed ISO/US date formats, quoted description with embedded comma, malformed rows mixed with valid ones (assert valid ones survive + error details), zero-amount and both-debit-and-credit-filled row errors, missing-required-column file-level exceptions, empty file, header-only file (no rows, no error).
- `TransactionRepositoryTest.java`: add a test for `addAll` — sequential ids continuing from prior state, single persist, reloads correctly.
- No JavaFX UI test — the codebase has no TestFX dependency or `*ViewTest.java` precedent for any view; verify the button manually.

## Critical files
- `personal-finance-app/pom.xml` — add commons-csv
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionDraft.java` — new
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionCsvImportException.java` — new
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionCsvImporter.java` — new
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionRepository.java` — add `addAll`
- `personal-finance-app/src/main/java/com/example/finance/TransactionEntryView.java` — add Import CSV button
- `personal-finance-app/src/test/java/com/example/finance/TransactionCsvImporterTest.java` — new
- `personal-finance-app/src/test/java/com/example/finance/TransactionRepositoryTest.java` — add `addAll` test

## Verification
```
cd "personal-finance-app"
mvn compile
mvn -Dtest=TransactionCsvImporterTest test
mvn -Dtest=TransactionRepositoryTest test
mvn test
mvn javafx:run
```
Manually, in the running app's Transactions tab:
- Import a CSV with `Date,Amount,Description,Category` headers, mixed +/- amounts, one bad-date row, one non-numeric-amount row — confirm the status summary and that valid rows appear.
- Import a CSV with `Transaction Date,Debit,Credit,Description` (no Category) — confirm rows show `Uncategorized` and correct income/expense types.
- Import a CSV with a quoted description containing a comma — confirm it isn't split into extra fields.
- Cancel the file picker — confirm no error.
- Import a garbage/empty file — confirm `Import failed: ...` shows and the app keeps running.
- Switch tabs and back — confirm summary totals reflect the import.
- Check `~/.personal-finance-app/data/transactions.txt` for sequential ids and correct persisted rows.

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>personal-finance-app</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <name>Personal Finance App</name>
    <description>Desktop awareness-budgeting app: category targets, savings goals, and long-term obligations</description>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.source>17</maven.compiler.source>
        <maven.compiler.target>17</maven.compiler.target>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
        <javafx.version>21.0.2</javafx.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.openjfx</groupId>
            <artifactId>javafx-controls</artifactId>
            <version>${javafx.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- JUnit 5 aggregate (API + Engine) for tests -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.11.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <release>${maven.compiler.source}</release>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.2.5</version>
                <configuration>
                    <useModulePath>false</useModulePath>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.openjfx</groupId>
                <artifactId>javafx-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>0.0.8</version>
                <configuration>
                    <mainClass>com.example.finance.MainApp</mainClass>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

## Summary

Implemented CSV transaction import for the Personal Finance App:

- **`pom.xml`** — added Apache Commons CSV 1.11.0
- **`TransactionDraft.java`** (new) — record carrying a row's parsed fields, minus id
- **`TransactionCsvImportException.java`** (new) — thrown only for whole-file problems (unreadable, empty, missing required columns)
- **`TransactionCsvImporter.java`** (new) — resolves header aliases (`Date`/`Transaction Date`, `Amount`/`Debit`+`Credit`, optional `Category`→`Uncategorized`), parses ISO or `M/d/yyyy` dates, infers income/expense from sign or debit/credit, and skips bad rows individually (collecting reasons) rather than aborting the whole import
- **`TransactionRepository.addAll(...)`** (new method) — bulk-inserts drafts with one file rewrite instead of N
- **`TransactionEntryView.java`** — new "Import CSV" button opens a `FileChooser`, imports, and reports a summary in the existing status label
- **Tests** — 13 new `TransactionCsvImporterTest` cases (aliasing, debit/credit, quoted commas, mixed date formats, malformed rows, ambiguous sign, missing columns, empty/header-only files) plus an `addAll` test in `TransactionRepositoryTest`

All 56 tests pass (`mvn test`), and `mvn javafx:run` starts without errors. Since the file-picker dialog is a native OS dialog, I couldn't click through it programmatically — I left two sample files at `/tmp/csv-import-test/sample1.csv` (signed Amount, one bad date, one bad amount, a quoted comma) and `sample2.csv` (Debit/Credit, no Category) for you to try via `mvn javafx:run` → Transactions tab → Import CSV.
